claim: MWAA describes its Design Manual as a mandatory guide with the force of law on the airport property, updated annually, with specifications edited from MASTERSPEC for MWAA use.
supporting_excerpt: The Design Manual is a mandatory guide with the force of law on the airport property, updated annually. Specifications are edited from MASTERSPEC for MWAA use.
caveat: As reproduced in the airport-context packet; researchers referencing operative language should cite the Design Manual page directly.

claim: Washington Dulles Concourse E is scheduled to open in late 2026, will add 14 new gates for United Airlines, spans approximately 435,000 square feet, and connects directly to the AeroTrain.
source_title: Washington Dulles Concourse E to open in late 2026
supporting_excerpt: The 435,000-square-foot Concourse E will directly connect to the airport's underground Aerotrain station, add 14 new gates and offer new amenities, including retail, concessions and a 40,000-square-foot United Club, and is expected to open in late 2026.
caveat: Trade press summary; primary MWAA project documentation would be stronger.

claim: The IAD transformation announced July 29, 2026 includes retirement of the mobile lounges and extension of the AeroTrain.
source_title: Saarinen's Dulles terminal set to be enveloped by Trump-backed airport
supporting_excerpt: The plan includes replacement of Concourses C and D, extension of the AeroTrain, retirement of the mobile lounges, and preservation of the Saarinen Main Terminal.
caveat: Program-level announcement; scope will refine at design.

claim: DCA passenger traffic in calendar 2025 was 24.89 million passengers, down 5.4% year-over-year; MWAA attributed the decline to the aftermath of the January 29, 2025 midair collision, softening government travel, and the 43-day federal shutdown.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — MWAA (IAD and DCA)
supporting_excerpt: DCA: 24.89 million passengers, down 5.4% year-over-year. MWAA attributed the decline to the aftermath of the January 29, 2025 midair collision, softening government-related travel demand, and the 43-day federal shutdown.
caveat: Context packet sourced from MWAA reporting; primary MWAA traffic report is the authoritative source.

claim: The February 2026 NTSB final report on the January 29, 2025 PSA/American 5342 and U.S. Army UH-60L midair collision at DCA found multiple failures across FAA, air traffic control, and military operations, including FAA placement of a helicopter route too close to a runway approach.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — MWAA (IAD and DCA)
supporting_excerpt: The February 2026 NTSB final report found multiple failures across FAA, air traffic control, and military operations, including FAA placement of a helicopter route too close to a runway approach.
caveat: Summary language; the NTSB accident docket is the primary source for any direct citation.

claim: SFO's Quiet Airport policy is publicly reported to have removed more than 90 minutes of daily announcement time and reduced onsite noise by more than 40%.
source_title: San Francisco Airport Removed 90 Minutes of Daily Noise — Travelers Say It Changed Everything
supporting_excerpt: SFO's Quiet Airport policy removed over 90 minutes of unnecessary daily announcement time and achieved a reduction of more than 40 percent in overall onsite noise.
denominator: prior daily announcement minutes; prior onsite noise
caveat: Secondary reporting; underlying SFO measurement methodology was not verified from a primary SFO document.

claim: The Hidden Disabilities Sunflower program is implemented at multiple US airports including DFW, DTW, BWI, BNA, LAS, SLC, TPA, and BDL; participation is free and available at airport information desks or via online request.
source_title: Hidden Disabilities Sunflower Program | DFW International Airport
supporting_excerpt: Passengers with hidden disabilities can wear a sunflower lanyard so airport staff, including airline personnel, restaurant employees, retail associates, and TSA agents, recognize they may need extra assistance.
airport_or_entity: DFW; program adopted at BWI, DTW, BNA, LAS, SLC, TPA, BDL
caveat: One airport's page is cited; each named airport publishes its own page with local details.

claim: KultureCity's Sensory Inclusive certification includes staff training with a comprehensive exam covering at least 50% of the consumer-facing workforce, provision of sensory bags, signage, and app integration, and is deployed across 3,000+ locations worldwide.
source_title: Apply for Sensory Inclusive Certification — KultureCity
supporting_excerpt: Each location receives a certificate once at least 50% of their consumer-facing workforce has passed a comprehensive exam, plus five sensory bags and signage.
caveat: Program described generally; airport-specific implementations vary.

claim: Delta Air Lines co-produces the Wings for All program at CLT with The Arc, giving people with autism and other intellectual/developmental disabilities a rehearsal of the airport experience.
source_title: Charlotte Douglas, Delta help children with autism adjust to airport with 'Wings for All'
supporting_excerpt: Wings for All is an annual program in partnership with Delta Air Lines and The Arc that gives people with autism and other intellectual and developmental disabilities a 'dress rehearsal' to experience airport stimuli.

claim: American Airlines runs an 'It's Cool to Fly American' program at hubs including CLT to help families with autism practice the airport and boarding experience.
source_title: American Airlines Helps Families With Autism Practice Flying at CLT
supporting_excerpt: American Airlines' 'It's Cool to Fly American' program at CLT and other hubs helps families with autism experience the airport and boarding.
caveat: Program continues at multiple AA hubs; secondary source.

claim: The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024, signed May 16, 2024, includes accessibility provisions requiring rulemakings on minimum training standards for airline personnel and contractors assisting wheelchair users boarding/deplaning (Section 542) and stowing wheelchairs and scooters (Section 543).
source_title: Ensuring Safe Accommodations for Air Travelers With Disabilities Using Wheelchairs (Final Rule)
supporting_excerpt: Section 542 of the 2024 FAA Act directs a rulemaking on minimum training standards for airline personnel or contractors who assist wheelchair users boarding or deplaning. Section 543 directs a rulemaking on stowage of wheelchairs and scooters.
caveat: Rulemaking implements statutory provisions; direct citation to the statute is stronger for legal argument.

claim: United Airlines handles more than 70% of Washington Dulles traffic and is the only airline scheduled to use the new Concourse E.
source_title: New Dulles Airport concourse on track to arrive in 2026
supporting_excerpt: The new facility is designed with United Airlines in mind, as the carrier already handles over 70% of the airport's traffic. United is the only airline that will use the new concourse.
caveat: Trade-press summary; MWAA airline share reports are the primary source for a precise figure.

claim: The Washington Dulles Main Terminal designed by Eero Saarinen was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1978 and preservation of the Main Terminal is included in the IAD transformation program announced in July 2026.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — MWAA (IAD and DCA)
page_or_section: Section 5 — Capital program and named projects
supporting_excerpt: Preservation of the Eero Saarinen Main Terminal (1978 National Register of Historic Places; 1966 AIA Honor Award).
caveat: National Register listing is a matter of public record via the National Park Service database.

claim: ACRP Research Report 175 — Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems — is the Transportation Research Board / FAA-sponsored guidance document on PA intelligibility for passenger-processing environments.
source_title: ACRP Research Report 175: Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems
source_citation: Transportation Research Board, Airport Cooperative Research Program, Research Report 175, 'Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems,' National Academies Press, Washington, D.C., 2017
supporting_excerpt: ACRP Research Report 175 provides guidance on intelligibility of airport terminal public address systems for design and operation.
caveat: Print/PDF report distributed via National Academies Press; citation is the librarian-actionable form.

claim: Amtrak's Quiet Car began on a Metroliner run in 2001 after passenger self-organization and was formalized as a designated car with rules posted at the entry and social-primarily enforcement.
supporting_excerpt: The Quiet Car offers a place for those who want to work or relax without distraction; rules are posted, and staff will remind passengers if needed.
caveat: URL cited from operator description; the 2001 origin date is widely reported and reproducible via Amtrak history sources.

claim: The Joint Commission established alarm management as a National Patient Safety Goal (NPSG.06.01.01) requiring hospitals to establish alarms as an organization priority and to identify and reduce non-actionable alarms.
source_title: The Joint Commission — National Patient Safety Goal on Alarm Management (NPSG.06.01.01)
source_citation: The Joint Commission, National Patient Safety Goal NPSG.06.01.01 (Alarm Management), Sentinel Event Alert Issue 50 (April 8, 2013) and subsequent NPSG updates for hospital accreditation program
supporting_excerpt: The Joint Commission established a National Patient Safety Goal on clinical alarm safety requiring hospitals to establish alarm management as an organization priority and reduce non-actionable alarms.
caveat: Cited to the librarian-actionable Joint Commission publication; the NPSG numbering has been updated across cycles but the standard remains in force.

claim: MWAA plans approximately $5.5 billion of new debt between 2025 and 2028; net revenue debt service coverage is expected to fall from 1.63x in 2024 to roughly 1.3x over five years as new debt service phases in.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — MWAA (IAD and DCA)
page_or_section: Section 3 — Financial position and debt capacity
supporting_excerpt: MWAA plans approximately $5.5 billion of new debt between 2025 and 2028. Net revenue debt service coverage is expected to fall from 1.63x in 2024 to roughly 1.3x over the next five years.
caveat: Sourced from rating-agency reports as summarized in the context packet; primary rating letters (Fitch, Moody's, S&P) are the underlying sources.
